text: せかい　じゅうに　すんでいる　ポケモンたちが　レッドを　まって　おるぞー！

structure.jp: せかい　じゅうに　すんでいる
レッドを　まって　おるぞー！

patterns.name: 〜ている
patterns.explanation: いる after a て-form verb says the action is going on now. おる is the old-man form of いる. まって　おる = 'are waiting'.

patterns.name: verb + noun
patterns.span: すんでいる　ポケモンたち
patterns.explanation: The phrase ending in a verb sits before a thing and tells you which ones. すんでいる　ポケモンたち = 'the Pokémon that live (there)'.

patterns.name: 〜ぞ
patterns.explanation: ぞ at the end is a rough, strong way of telling someone something, used mostly by men. おるぞー = 'they are, I tell you!'.
